technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: Surplus-value arises from variable capital alone.
Machinery, like every other component of constant capital, creates no new value.
Surplus-value arises from variable capital alone.
The value of labour-power was determined by the labour-time needed to maintain the worker and family.
Capital loses both use-value and exchange-value when it loses contact with living labour.
A machine loses exchange-value when cheaper or better machines compete with it.
Value of a machine is set by the labour-time needed to reproduce it.
Machinery produces relative surplus-value by cheapening labour-power and raising productiveness.
The analysis of absolute surplus-value assumed intensity as given.
Surplus labour compared with necessary labour, in a ratio of 100%.
Surplus labour is the labour beyond the part that pays the worker's wages.
Rate of surplus-value is set by the ratio of surplus to necessary labour in the day.
Early machine products sell above their individual value, which gives extra profit.
Machinery enters the labour-process as a whole but the value-process only in parts.
Machinery enters the value-begetting process only by bits.
Productiveness of machinery is inversely proportional to the value it transfers to the product.
Material wear and tear is of two kinds: from use and from non-use.
A machine loses value through cheaper or better rivals even while still sound.
Once hours are cut, capital pushes more work into each hour.
Labour gains a measure of intensity as well as duration when the day is shortened.
Machinery frees a surplus working population that capital can command.
Factory growth fixes a rising share of capital in machinery, which only pays while it runs.
Machinery alters the composition of capital, so less is laid out on labour-power.
The productiveness of a machine is measured by the human labour-power it replaces.
Machinery cuts workers off from their means of subsistence, which economists call setting them free.
The value of machinery is the means of production plus mechanics' wages and surplus-value.
In the automatic factory the skill of the worker passes over to the machine.
Only in the factory system does the tool come to employ the workman.
Manufacturers reduced the piece-wage as well as the number of days worked.
Shows that workers can be swapped without stopping a machine-run process.
Barrack discipline develops the labour of overlooking to a full system.
Workers in reserve move into new branches as machinery frees men in one branch.
Marx asks whether any capital is set free by the change to machinery.
Machines do their work gratuitously, like natural forces, after allowing for wear and tear.
